references.text: In Matthew's parallel account, the whole town asks Jesus to leave their region, corresponding to the crowd's plea in Luke 8:37.
Mark's parallel account tells that the people began to ask Jesus to leave their region after the healing of the demon-possessed man.
The Philistines sent away the ark of the covenant because they feared the Lord's power, similarly to how the people in the Gerasene region asked Jesus to leave due to great fear.
Peter asks Jesus to go away from him because he is a sinful man—a similar reaction of fear and awe toward God's power.
The authorities in Philippi asked Paul and Silas to leave the city, a parallel to how the people asked Jesus to depart.
Just before this in context, the disciples were afraid and said, 'Who is he?', showing the consistent reaction of fear toward Jesus' mighty works.
The crowd's fear in verse 37 is a direct response to what they heard and saw in verses 35–36, where the healed man was sitting clothed and in his right mind.
Matthew's parallel describes the demon-possessed men as so dangerous that no one could pass by—this underscores the background for the great fear the people felt.
